title: Retention Manual/Scheduled Run Mutual-Exclusion Race

discoveredBy.jobName: ci-layers / Layer 5: full-suite/compatibility fail-safe (backend, legacy server:test DB-required members)

failingAssertion.testName: concurrent live runs: the shared job lock serializes execution — only one run actually deletes; both attempts get their own started+terminal audit pair, the loser terminal is manual_run_blocked/concurrent_run_in_progress
failingAssertion.assertionMessage: exactly one concurrent live run must execute (200) and the other must be rejected as already-in-progress (409)

rootCause.summary: jobLock.ts's acquire/release primitive is atomic and race-free (empirically stress-tested: 130 concurrent-acquisition trials against real PostgreSQL with the production Prisma 7.8.0 + @prisma/adapter-pg driver-adapter stack, 0 double-grants). The actual defect is structural ordering in platformAdmin.ts's manual-run route: the shared JobLock was acquired only AFTER two other variable-latency DB round trips (getPlatformSetting policy-gate read, recordManualRunStarted audit-write transaction) that both racers perform independently. Because live-run cleanup against a small dataset completes in single-digit milliseconds, a fast racer's entire acquire-cleanup-release cycle could finish before a simultaneously-fired second racer even reached its own lock attempt, letting both legitimately (sequentially, not concurrently) acquire the lock and both return 200.

fix.jobLockChanges: acquireJobLock and releaseJobLock exported (were private, internal to withJobLock). withJobLock itself unchanged, still used unchanged by the scheduled cron and every other job in the codebase.
fix.routeChanges: POST /privacy/data-retention/run live-run branch now calls acquireJobLock() first, before recordManualRunStarted(); both winner and loser still write their own started row (audit-shape contract unchanged); loser branches directly to blocked terminal + 409 with no cleanup call; cleanup wrapped in try/finally releasing the lock on success, throw, or any other exit; a NEW edge case (lock acquired, then started-write fails) releases the lock before returning 500.

testsAddedOrStrengthened.name: race gate: 10 consecutive concurrent live-run rounds against real PostgreSQL — zero double-success, zero double-block observations
acquireJobLock(): N-way (4) truly-concurrent acquisition on a fresh lock name grants to exactly one caller
acquireJobLock()/releaseJobLock(): after release, the lock is immediately free again — no orphaning after a normal successful completion
acquireJobLock()/releaseJobLock(): a try/finally around a throwing callback (mirroring the route's cleanup wrapper) still releases the lock — no orphan after a thrown exception
lock acquired but the "started" audit write then fails: the lock is released immediately, not orphaned for its full TTL
scheduled/manual lock collision: a live manual run is rejected 409 when the shared lock is already held...
addedAssertions: seeded eligible row is untouched after the 409 (no cleanup performed)
the simulated scheduled-cron's lock ownership (lockedBy) is untouched by the rejected manual attempt

regressionCommands.result: server:test:disposable-db exit 0, cleanup succeeded, zero residual docker resources

securityTenantKvkk.auditImpact: every attempt (winner, loser, and both new failure edge-cases) still writes the required started/terminal audit pair with correct action/outcome/errorCategory; no audit row newly lost or duplicated
securityTenantKvkk.kvkkImpact: closes a real (though never observed to cause actual double-deletion) concurrent-execution risk in manual retention triggers, directly relevant to retention operational integrity
securityTenantKvkk.concurrentDeletionRiskExisted: narrow sense only: sequential-but-not-overlapping double execution was possible pre-fix; true simultaneous deletion of the same rows was always prevented by the already-atomic lock (proven in root-cause investigation)
